shortName: Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences F. Edward Hebert School of Medicine

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Our institution is committed to fostering an optimal learning environment by supporting interest groups developed by students. We provide broad-based educational programming, mentorship initiatives, and leadership development opportunities. We also support interest groups open to all members of our community, facilitating professional development, cultural engagement, and collaborative learning that align with our mission to develop well-rounded military medical professionals. Of note, participation in interest groups is not restricted by any protected characteristic.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Since students are active duty officers during medical school, they must adhere to the regulations governing military members for a leave of absence.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The School has a wide variety of organizations and activities representing the interests of our students and faculty. Our medical specialty interest groups provide our student body with opportunities to interact with physicians and patients early in their medical school careers. Sporting and creative arts groups provide students with opportunities to express their talents while keeping them connected to pursuits they love. Our medical school features unique military activities, like the Operational Medicine Group and Humanitarian Assistance & Disaster Medicine Group that help develop our students as medical officers. Students serve on each of our school’s standing committees and are involved in all aspects of University life.
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
Our university is located outside the Nation's Capital, across the street from the National Institutes of Health. We are located near public transportation, shopping, and dining, and there are many cultural and recreational opportunities for our students to enjoy.  Studying for medical school will certainly take up a lot of time, but the Metropolitan Washington D.C. area provides countless opportunities for unique experiences in an area rich with culture and history.

After the first sixteen months, students at the School conduct required rotations by lottery at sites all across the United States, including Virginia, North Carolina, Georgia, Ohio, Texas, California, Washington and Hawaii, among others. In the last eighteen months, students frequently take advantage of global electives while preparing for internship. USU offers a national and international medical school experience!
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Students are provided a non-taxable housing allowance (for the rank of an 0-1-regardless of prior service) to defray the costs of living in the Metropolitan Washington DC area. Rates for 2026 are $3054.00 per month for students who are unmarried and without children, $3213.00 per month for students who are married and/or have children. Due to its location on the Metro Red Line, students choose to live in a variety of places in Maryland, Virginia, and DC. This housing allowance is in addition to the $4150.00 basic pay that our students receive each month (more for those with prior military experience).
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: We offer confidential counseling, wellness resources, and mentorship opportunities designed to support the personal and professional growth of all students. Additionally, our institution provides person centered health education and leadership development programs that promote collaboration and excellence while ensuring that all students have access to the same opportunities for success.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The Well-Being Program, a recent addition to the student support network, focuses on improving resilience and helping students cope with stress by facilitating student-faculty mentorship, peer-to-peer networking, volunteering, and social and community activities. For more information: https://www.usuhs.edu/node/63018
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Our student body is comprised of some of our nation’s brightest scholars, those with a profound curiosity and commitment to service, science, and the greater good. We work hard to foster a supportive environment where students flourish both academically and socially. A pervasive spirit of camaraderie and teamwork distinguishes USU from other universities. Whether it’s playing on an intramural sports team, studying with friends in the library, or just hanging out with classmates in the Student Union, there are many social outlets at USU. Student groups, volunteer opportunities, mentorship programs, special guest lecturers, and so much more bring our student body together in new and exciting ways every day. Other student benefits, such as academic counselors, study groups, and student government organizations help to enrich the USU experience and provide students with the tools and resources needed to succeed.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Most students take public transportation to the Medical Center Metro stop where a shuttle to USU is available. A SmarTrip metro pass that can be used for both rail and bus transportation can be purchased from the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority. Fares, bus and rail maps, and trip planners can be found at wmata.com. Service members can be reimbursed for Metro costs up to $325 per month (approximate), based on individual commuter costs.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students are required to wear the Uniform of the Day while on campus or on rotation.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Office hours are flexible and in addition to a robust array of counseling and student support services, USU also offers an Academic Success Program that is available to all students free of charge.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students begin working with patients on the second day of medical school and continue to work with patients throughout the entire medical curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Instruction includes a mix of lectures, labs, small groups, clinical practice, and simulation. Clerkships and clinical electives are conducted at military treatment facilities worldwide.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical clerkships begin during the second half of the second year of medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Students without prior qualifying officer service experience must complete their service specific orientation program during the summer before actually matriculating into the School of Medicine.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Students are not ranked at this school.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Lectures are optional and almost all lectures are pre-recorded with video capture technology.  Attendance is required for labs and small group sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The School of Medicine at the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences (aka USU or “America’s Medical School”) bases its curriculum on the theme of "Molecules to Military Medicine." The curriculum incorporates four key conceptual pillars: The integration of basic & clinical sciences throughout all four years, early patient contact, adaptability to unique learning styles, and the use of advanced educational technologies to promote student learning and development. 

The medical school curriculum underwent a full-scale revision in 2011 which included a shift from a traditional, discipline or course-based curriculum, to an integrated, organ-system based approach, allowing medical science to be learned and applied in a clinical context. The expanding use of artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly allows for more personalized educational development and is being actively incorporated in all phases of the curriculum. Students start interacting with real and/or simulated patients within the first few weeks of class while continuing to study and master those aspects of the basic sciences that represent the foundation of all medical education.

The curriculum itself is divided into three main phases:  An 18-month pre-clerkship period, a 12-month core clerkship period, and a 16-month post-clerkship period.  Included in the early part of the post-clerkship period is a 6-week segment known as “Bench to Bedside and Beyond.” During this section of the curriculum students have an opportunity to re-visit salient aspects of the basic sciences in a clinically focused context, learn the fundamental skills associated with Advanced Life Support (ALS) and earn official certification in Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS).  The post-clerkship period includes time for advanced electives, audition rotations, research and at least two sub-internships. All students must take and pass USMLE Step 1 and Step 2 prior to graduation.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: USU offers a unique learning experience blending science with commitment to service. Primary care is highly valued; over 40% of our graduating students choose careers in Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, or OB/GYN each year. In addition to delivering the core medical education offered at other medical schools, The curriculum includes an additional 700 hrs of military content applicable to a broad array of future primary care or subspecialty physicians. Multi-disciplinary lectures, labs, and clinical skills training are a central part of the pre-clinical curriculum and are combined with educationally aligned military medical training and field exercises interspersed throughout all four years. The curriculum gives students a strong foundation in military-medical leadership coupled with training in acute trauma/disaster management. This blend of military-medical training gives graduates the skills necessary to provide quality medical care in austere/challenging environments.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
USU is the innovation hub for the Military Health System. The university and medical school are committed to transformative research that delivers products to improve the lives of service members, their families and retired beneficiaries, and that meet the needs of the Department of War. USU and the Military Health System are supported by more than $1 billion of medical research investment.

Academic departments and Centers at USU have collaborations with the NIH, the Veterans Administration, and other military and civilian labs which afford many scholarly opportunities for our students. USU has an international faculty performing cutting edge research in the fields of infectious disease, trauma, rehabilitation, radiation exposure and brain injury. Students able to balance the rigors of undergraduate medical education and research may choose to tackle longer-term projects during their post-clerkship period.

For more information, view our website at https://www.usuhs.edu/overview
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Students complete 7 integrated, organ-based modules spread across an 18-month pre-clerkship curriculum. Clerkship rotations are conducted at U.S. sites and post-clerkship electives can be world-wide.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students serve as Military, Public Health Service or Coast Guard officers while attending school.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Strongly encouraged; included as a component of the newly instituted Capstone Project.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Students receive part of their clinical training at a number of teaching hospitals affiliated with the university in Maryland, Virginia, Texas, California, and Hawaii among others.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Coursework is graded on an Honors/Pass/Fail basis.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Created by public law in 1972, the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences (USU) was founded to prepare men and women of all backgrounds for careers as health care professionals in the Military, Public Health Service and Coast Guard. The School of Medicine provides a comprehensive education to select individuals who demonstrate potential for, and commitment to, careers as medical officers caring for the service-members, retirees, and families that have served our nation.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The Uniformed Services University School of Medicine trains Army, Navy, Air Force, Coast Guard, and PHS physicians, public health practitioners, psychologists, and biomedical scientists to support our nation’s military and public health systems, the National Security and Defense Strategies of the United States, and the readiness of our Uniformed Services. As the Leadership Academy of Military Medicine, we prepare our students to become outstanding clinical practitioners, researchers, and leaders.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks. Deferments are rarely given and typically only granted due to circumstances beyond the control of the applicant.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: If you are not able to furnish any of the required letters, please send in the letters you have, along with an explanation about why you are unable to obtain the missing required letter(s).
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: If your undergraduate, post baccalaureate, or graduate institution has a pre-medical committee that produces a letter of recommendation, then that letter, in addition to a letter from someone that has viewed you in a patient care setting, is sufficient to meet the requirement.  Otherwise, please submit two letters from professors in the natural sciences, one from a professor in a different field, and one letter from a writer that has worked with you in a clinical setting. Even if you have been out of school for an extended period of time, you must still attempt to submit academic letters of recommendation.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Applicants who are selected for an interview will be notified by email.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Applications are reviewed as they are received, and the first interview invitations are sent in mid-late July. Interview invitations will continue to be offered through early December.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Each candidate for admission has two individual thirty-minute interviews. These interviews are conducted by our current medical students and active or retired military medical officers.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews for the MD and MD/PhD programs will be held virtually for the 2026-2027 cycle.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: applicants will be emailed a link to the secondary and will complete the application in WebAdMIT.
medSchoolApplication.secApplEarliestDtText: without an MCAT or all of the letters of recommendation; however, both components are required to be considered for an interview.
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: Applicants must submit the secondary application within three weeks of being notified of its availability. Deadline extensions will not be granted without prior approval.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: Applicants must have a demonstrated strong performance in all areas.  A minimum MCAT score of 505 and a science GPA of 3.5 is required. https://medschool.usuhs.edu/academics/early-decision-program
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Students must be citizens of the United States.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: State of residence is not taken into account.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Applicants must be U.S. citizens as they will serve as commissioned officers.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: Applicants must be U.S. citizens as they will serve as commissioned officers.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: Information about our Admissions policies and procedures can be found at: https://medschool.usuhs.edu/admissions/application-requirements
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Although the minimum GPA is a 3.0 for consideration, the average GPA for matriculants is a 3.7.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Community college courses are accepted as long as the applicant possess a baccalaureate degree from a U.S. accredited university or college.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: The USU Admissions Committee welcomes any updates that will aid them in their decision.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The USU School of Medicine prepares ethical, highly competent physicians committed to "caring for those in harm’s way" and other Military Health System beneficiaries. Towards that end, we select applicants who demonstrate great potential as physicians and leaders and who demonstrate a strong commitment to the advancement of military medicine and public health, by fulfilling a promise of duty and expertise. Our educational program ensures students meet the General Competencies and Milestones of the American Board of Medical Specialties and ACGME, pass the USMLE components required for licensure, and integrate the principles of officership, leadership, knowledge, skills, attitudes, and overall professionalism expected of uniformed medical officers.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: USU does not charge tuition. Upon entering the first-year class of the School of Medicine, students are commissioned as Second Lieutenants in the Army or Air Force or as Ensigns in the Navy, Public Health Service or Coast Guard, receiving the pay and benefits of that grade (including health insurance).  At graduation, students are promoted to the rank of Captain in the Air Force or Army or the rank of Lieutenant in the Navy, Public Health Service or Coast Guard upon receipt of the M.D. degree. Graduates are obligated to serve as active duty medical officers for not less than seven years. The period of time spent in internship or residency training does not satisfy the seven-year obligation (although it does count for purposes of retirement). Those physicians who complete 20 years or more on active duty are eligible for a military retirement, including monthly compensation and health benefits.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: There are no tuition or fees associated with attending the University.  Medical books and equipment are provided to all students.  As a result, graduates are obligated to serve as active duty officers for not less than seven years. Time spent in internship or residency training does not satisfy the seven-year obligation. Student dropped from the program for any reason may be required to perform active duty service for a period of time equal to the time spent in the program. A disenrolled student may be required to reimburse the government for tuition and fees.

medSchoolPrograms.info: Students admitted into the MD/PhD Program will be commissioned officers for the duration of the seven-year program. These students will incur an additional service obligation beyond the standard seven-year obligation for the MD Program.

The Enlisted to Medical Degree Preparatory Program (EMDP2) is a partnership between the Uniformed Services University and Armed Forces. This 24 month program is only offered to enlisted service members from the Army, Navy, Air Force, Coast Guard and Marine Corps.  The program enables highly qualified enlisted service members to complete the preparatory coursework for application to medical school while maintaining an active duty status. (Contact Dr. Lisa Harris)

The USU Summer Scholars Program is an 8 to 10-week training program that provides unique exposure to basic and clinical research, social/behavioral research, health policy, and research administration to high school and college students.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Applicants can select the Plan to Enroll option.

Beginning April 30, accepted applicants will have the option to select: “Commit to Enroll.” Selecting this option indicates that you have made a final selection and withdrawn all other applications. “Commit to Enroll” does not automatically withdraw applications from other medical schools. Applicants must communicate directly with all schools about their final decision.

medSchoolAssessments.assessmentAdditionalInformation: USU Recommends taking the exam; however, applicants can submit their application with or without a PREview score.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: USU uses rolling admissions. Offers can be tendered to those wait list applicants if a position becomes available.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Students wishing to apply to the School of Medicine must complete one-year each of Biology, General Chemistry, and Physics with lab. Students must also complete one-year of Organic Chemistry with lab; or one semester of Organic Chemistry with lab and one semester of Biochemistry. Students are also required to complete one year of English, Foreign Language, Writing Intensive Humanities, Social Science, or Psychology courses. Also, one semester of *Calculus or Statistics is required. Advanced Placement and International Baccalaureate courses for which one's college or university has granted credit are acceptable for these requirements. CLEP will not be accepted for the prerequisites.  *For the 2028 FYC, one semester of Calculus will be required. Coursework must be completed by 1 June of the year of matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The school employs a three-stage, progressive selection process. The first stage consists of the submission of an AMCAS application; the second, the submission of supplementary materials; and the third, personal interviews. Advancement in the process is competitive, based on candidates' personal and intellectual characteristics. The Admissions Committee does not discriminate on the basis of sex, race, color, creed, religion, national origin, marital status, or other federally protected classes.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: After verifying minimum academic criteria, the Admissions Committee values clinical exposure and community service.  Although there is no minimum number of hours that must be spent in the clinical setting or volunteering, the Admissions looks for experiences that promotes personal growth.
